findings.claim: The 'master formula' (tilted explicit formula) is stated as an unconditional identity for all a > 1/2, but it is exact only above sup{beta}; below, it omits discrete Plemelj jump terms for every zero to the right of the tilted line — i.e., as stated it silently assumes the very quasi-RH(a) it is meant to certify.
findings.argument: Both sides re-derived. LHS := Sigma_rho m_rho (P_{a-beta} * w)(gamma) equals int w(t) u(a+it) dt for every a not equal to some beta (Hadamard identity, paired convergence). RHS := Arch_a(w) - Sigma_{n<=X} Lambda(n) n^{-a} c-hat_w(log n) is real-analytic (entire) in a, and equality LHS = RHS holds for a > 1 by the absolutely convergent Dirichlet series of zeta'/zeta (no mirror term needed there — correct). But the single term I(a) = m int P_{a-beta0}(t-gamma0) w(t) dt is DISCONTINUOUS at a = beta0: int P_x(y) w(gamma0+y) dy -> +pi*w(gamma0) as x->0+ and -> -pi*w(gamma0) as x->0-, a jump of 2*pi*m*w(gamma0). Equivalently, the natural EF test W(rho) = (1/pi) int w(t)/((a+it)-rho) dt is a Cauchy transform of w dt on the line Re s = a and has a Plemelj jump across it, so it is NOT a single analytic function on the strip and the Weil EF does not apply verbatim. Hence for a in (1/2, 1) the correct unconditional identity is LHS = RHS - 2*pi*Sigma_{rho: beta > a} m_rho w(gamma_rho) (up to the exact normalization of the jump). The omission matters concretely: milestone M3's LP/certificates consume this formula to constrain zero configurations from prime data; in an RH-false world the constraint set as written is simply wrong, and any 'certified' quasi-RH(a) box built on the stated identity would be unsound. Repair is standard EF bookkeeping and even helpful — for w >= 0 the correction is sign-definite and IS the detector — but the field's 'identity backbone' must be restated before anything is built on it.

findings.claim: Corollary T2 of the first theorem is false as stated: certified positivity of u on the SINGLE segment {sigma = a, |t| <= T} is not equivalent (up to t-edge collars) to quasi-RH(a) up to height T. Deep off-line zeros are invisible on a shallow segment.
findings.argument: The anchoring direction (quasi-RH(a) => u > 0 on the segment, up to C1/(a-1/2) edge collars) is fine. The converse fails: a zero rho0 = beta0 + i*gamma0 with beta0 substantially greater than a contributes only -(beta0-a)/((beta0-a)^2) = -1/(beta0-a) at the nearest point of the segment sigma = a, while the ambient on-line positivity there is Sigma_gamma P_{a-1/2}(t-gamma) ~ pi * density = (1/2) log(gamma0/2pi). Numerically: beta0 = 0.9, a = 0.55, gamma0 = 10^6 gives negative term -2.86 against ambient ~ +6.0 — u stays strictly positive on the whole segment while quasi-RH(0.55) is badly false. Any zero at depth beta0 > a + 2/log(gamma0) is invisible on the segment. This is not a subtle point: the proposal's OWN failure-mode-3 text says negativity plumes hug sigma ~ beta0 with width ~ 1/((beta-a) log gamma), which directly contradicts the single-segment equivalence claimed in T2 and echoed in M3 and the Lean hook. Repair: quasi-RH(a) boxes require certified positivity on a sigma-GRID of segments from a up to ~1 with spacing ~ 1/log T (about log T lines), which multiplies certification cost by log T but preserves the concept. The 'single harmonic function on one segment' slogan must go; note there is no maximum-principle rescue, since u -> -infinity on the left side of any interior zero, defeating boundary-positivity arguments.

findings.claim: The central formal object of the field — the Pontryagin index ladder kappa_a with its Krein-Langer negative-squares theory, jump formulas, and defect ('ghost') spaces — is not known to be well-defined (finite) for zeta at ANY rung a < 1, and is genuinely infinite for the Davenport-Heilbronn model that milestone M2 proposes as its validation instance.
findings.argument: kappa_a = #{rho : beta > a} counted over ALL heights. Unconditionally, nothing known excludes infinitely many zeros to the right of any fixed vertical line sigma = a < 1 (zero-density bounds give N(sigma,T) << T^{c(1-sigma)}, which is compatible with kappa_a = infinity for every a in (1/2,1)). Krein-Langer factorization and the entire Pontryagin-space apparatus (finite negative squares, finite-dimensional defect space, Sylvester-inertia bookkeeping via RHLinalg) require kappa < infinity; 'kappa_a < infinity for all a > 1/2' is itself an open zero-clustering statement of RH-adjacent flavor, nowhere flagged in the proposal. Worse for M2: Davenport-Heilbronn has INFINITELY many zeros in sigma > 1 (classical, 1936), so the proposed validation model 'DH as an indefinite model with kappa > 0 at rung one' is a Krein-space (infinite-index) situation, not a Pontryagin one — the OS_kappa axioms as drafted (finite defect) cannot even be instantiated on it. Repairs: (i) define the ladder as N-union-{infinity}-valued and restrict the defect theory to the hypothesis kappa_a < infinity (or to height-truncated kernels); (ii) replace the DH validation model with a planted-single-zero Beurling model (kappa = 1) from the campaign's barrier-checker zoo; (iii) state explicitly that the rung statements TRP(a) (kappa_a = 0) are unaffected, since emptiness needs no finiteness theory — the k > 0 sector of the axiom system is what is at risk of vacuity.

findings.claim: The S2 obstruction-evasion ('broken by a SINGLE off-line zero') conflates the ideal field u (pointwise single-zero-sensitive, true) with the accessible certificate class (windowed prime-computable data at fixed X, plausibly NOT single-zero-rigid at height T) — the same ideal-vs-visible gap that emptied the campaign's negative-index route.
findings.argument: Pointwise, one off-line zero forces u -> -infinity from the left: S2 holds for the ideal object. But every prime-computable certificate in the design reads WINDOWED level-a data with t-resolution ~ 1: X = e^{2pi/width}, so width-1 windows need X ~ 535, while resolving plume scale (width ~ 1/log T in t, collar ~ 1/log T in sigma) needs log X ~ 2pi log T, i.e. X ~ T^{2pi} — prime sums of length T^c, exactly the classical visibility wall (transcript pp. 31-35: L*_ann ~ log(t0/2pi)^{0.89}). At O(1) resolution, an off-line zero shifts each windowed datum by an O(1) jump term (finding 1) against main terms of size log T contributed by ~log T on-line zeros per window; an adversary can plausibly absorb the discrepancy by displacing on-line zeros by ~1/log T each — so the windowed data class is likely NOT single-zero-rigid as T -> infinity, and the honest S2 status of the METHOD (as opposed to the field) is open. The proposal deserves credit for partially acknowledging this (failure mode 3, and the M3 calibrator is precisely the right cheap early test — the depth-direction analogue of the 256-law), but the Obstruction-evasion section overstates the current state: S2 is proven for the field, conjectural for anything computable. The depth-CM generator (G2) is the one genuinely new lever against this (sigma-profile rigidity across all a simultaneously via Hausdorff-moment constraints is a data coordinate the bandwidth ceilings do not parametrize — that claim I verified against the map's scope caveats and it is correct), but its detection power is exactly what M3 must measure before anything downstream is credited.

findings.claim: Novelty audit: the proposal is a new COMBINATION of known objects, not a new object; its nearest neighbors are undercounted. Suzuki's canonical-system program and Kaltenbäck-Woracek's indefinite Hermite-Biehler theory cover the tilt family and its (indefinite) de Branges structure, and the anchoring dichotomy is known-in-spirit in explicit zero-free-region practice.
findings.argument: Named neighbors it does cite (Lagarias 1999, Conrey-Li, Connes-Consani, Suzuki 2301.00421, dlVP lineage) are handled honestly. Missing: (i) M. Suzuki's canonical-systems papers (e.g. 'Hamiltonians arising from L-functions in the Selberg class', J. Funct. Anal. ~2021, and predecessors ~2016-2019) construct de Branges/HB structure for precisely the family xi(s + omega)-type tilts, including unconditional HB at deep tilt and 'RH iff HB for all tilts' — the tilt family and both endpoint facts of the ladder are latent there, not just in Lagarias 2005-06; (ii) Kaltenbäck-Woracek, 'Pontryagin spaces of entire functions I-VI' (IEOT 1999-2010), IS the indefinite Hermite-Biehler / Krein-Langer index machinery for E with kappa zeros in C+ — the 'index ladder' object is their theory evaluated along a one-parameter family; (iii) indefinite/Krein-space readings of RH positivity exist (Yoshida 1992, Bombieri 2000 — both already in the artifact's Appendix C.3 notes); (iv) the anchoring theorem is a quantitative converse-Landau statement of the kind used implicitly throughout explicit-ZFR work (Kadiri-style Re zeta'/zeta inequalities; Titchmarsh Thm 9.6 gives the local zero-sum representation), so an expert will read the first theorem as 'a clean packaging of known local analysis', publishable but not deep. What survives as genuinely unclaimed territory: the negativity-body {u <= 0} as a geometric object, the margin law m(a,T), depth-direction complete monotonicity as a constraint system, prime-computable windowed certificates at tilted lines, and the OS_kappa organization. Verdict: new combination + new organizing program; no evidence of a refuted idea resurfacing (tx_048 dropped the tilt for compression reasons the proposal genuinely inverts); 'we tried that in 19XX' applies only in the sobering sense that every rung quasi-RH(a), a < 1, is the 130-year-open zero-free-vertical-strip problem — the ladder reframes the difficulty, it does not reduce it, and the proposal's own failure mode 1 (archimedean drift ~ (1/2) log t per unit descent, Lindelof-adjacent) correctly prices the horizon.

findings.claim: The 'Lean-verified first rung' claim carries unstated fine print, and the M3 flagship deliverable is content-redundant against the computational verification frontier.
findings.argument: (i) ZeroFree.lean line 396 proves Re xi'/xi(sigma+it) >= N_T/(8t^2) only for 1 <= sigma <= 2 AND |t| >= max(2, 2T); instantiating T = |t|/2 does give unconditional positivity on the strip 1 <= sigma <= 2, |t| >= 2, but sigma > 2 (easy) and |t| < 2 (verified computation) are not formalized — 'the a >= 1 rung is ALREADY Lean-verified' should read 'verified on 1 <= sigma <= 2, |t| >= 2'. (ii) M3's showcase ('no zeros with beta > 0.9, |t| <= 10^3, from primes < 10^4 alone') is subsumed mathematically by Platt-Trudgian's rigorous RH verification to height 3*10^12 (literature.md section 9): as knowledge about zeta it is empty below that height. Its real value is methodological (demonstrating prime-side sufficiency of the tilted-EF data) and formal (a Lean-certified zero-free box would be a first — the Turing method is not formalized anywhere, and the EnclOK pattern makes this a credible first formalized zero-localization). The payoff section should price it as instrument-validation plus formalization-first, not as a zero-free-box 'theorem genre'; the open question of whether such boxes scale past verified heights with sub-polynomial X is exactly finding 4.

repairs: All four major findings are repairable without touching the field's architecture. (1) Restate the master formula unconditionally: Sigma_rho m_rho (P_{a-beta}*w)(gamma) = Arch_a(w) - Sigma_{n<=X} Lambda(n) n^{-a} c-hat_w(log n) - 2pi Sigma_{beta > a} m_rho w(gamma_rho); for w >= 0 the correction is sign-definite, so it can be carried as a nonnegative unknown in every M3 LP (and it IS the detector — a feature once stated). (2) Replace T2's single segment by a sigma-grid {sigma = a + j/log T} up to sigma ~ 1 (about log T segments per box); all certification claims, the Lean second target, and M3's box deliverable inherit a log T cost factor and survive. (3) Define the ladder as N-union-{infinity}-valued; gate the entire kappa > 0 defect/ghost/jump-formula sector of OS_kappa behind an explicit finiteness hypothesis (or work with height-truncated kernels, where finiteness is free); swap the M2 validation model from Davenport-Heilbronn (kappa = infinity in sigma > 1) to a planted-single-zero Beurling model (kappa = 1) from the barrier-checker zoo, keeping DH only as the rung-one S1 separator, which is its correct role. (4) Downgrade the S2 evasion claim to 'proven for the field, open for the certificate class', and promote the M3 calibrator + LP detection-power experiment from milestone to GATE: no M4 work until the calibrator either fails to match tilted-EF data (method has depth rigidity) or succeeds (field is bounded the way bandwidth methods are — itself the publishable delimitation theorem the sponsor wants). (5) Add to every M4-candidate inequality the standing requirement that the depth-CM generator G2 (Lambda >= 0) be load-bearing — G1 (RP/OS) alone consumes only FE + Hadamard, which DH satisfies, so any G1-only inequality is DH-barred a priori. (6) Novelty section: add Suzuki's canonical-system papers and Kaltenbäck-Woracek I-VI, and soften 'no publication studies...' accordingly. With these repairs the near-term program (M1 within months, M2-M3 as instrument-building plus the gate) is sound, honest, and worth running; the horizon remains as the designer prices it (~0.1 or less).
literature_flags: Lagarias, 'On a positivity property of the Riemann xi-function', Acta Arith. 89 (1999): load-bearing for the framing and the first theorem's context; statement (unconditional positivity on sigma >= 1; RH iff positivity on sigma > 1/2) is almost certainly correct but the exact form must be pulled and cited, not recalled.

Lagarias (~2005-06) Hermite-Biehler property of xi(a - iz) for a >= 1 (likely 'Hilbert spaces of entire functions and Dirichlet L-functions', Frontiers in Number Theory, Physics, and Geometry I): recalled from memory in tx_048 and re-recalled here; verify.

M. Suzuki, canonical systems / 'Hamiltonians arising from L-functions in the Selberg class' (J. Funct. Anal. ~2021) and predecessors: NOT cited by the proposal but appears to cover the tilt family's HB/de Branges structure including both endpoint facts of the ladder; must be audited before any novelty claim about the tilt family is published.

Kaltenbäck-Woracek, 'Pontryagin spaces of entire functions I-VI' (IEOT 1999-2010): the indefinite Hermite-Biehler / Krein-Langer index theory the ladder relies on; needed both for correctness (bounded-type and FINITENESS hypotheses of Krein-Langer) and for novelty attribution.

Krein-Langer factorization applied to Theta_a = xi(1-a-iz)/xi(a-iz): requires Theta_a of bounded type in C+ (plausible from order 1, must be written out) AND finitely many negative squares — the finiteness is open for zeta at every a < 1 (finding 3).

Trudgian's explicit S(t) bound (|S(t)| <= 0.112 log t + 0.278 loglog t + const): real lineage (Trudgian 2014; successor Hasanalizade-Shen-Wong 2021 with |S(t)| <= 0.1101 log t + ...); exact constants load-bearing for M1's window-count and must be taken from the paper.

Davenport-Heilbronn 1936 (and Epstein class number > 1): zeros in sigma > 1 — classical and correct; but the proposal additionally needs the COUNT of such zeros (infinitely many) for the M2 model discussion, which is what breaks the Pontryagin framing (finding 3).
Ford's effective Vinogradov-Korobov (Proc. LMS 2002): real; explicit constants needed for corollary T1's instantiation.
Levinson-Montgomery (1974) / Speiser (1935): correctly cited as nearest relatives concerning zeta' rather than the negativity body; fine.

findings.claim: The master 'tilted explicit formula' — the field's declared identity backbone — is false as stated for any level a below the depth of any zero in the window; its validity at level a is equivalent to the very rung quasi-RH(a) it is meant to prove, and the correction term is exactly the X^{depth} visibility blow-up of the obstruction canon.
findings.argument: The proposal states: for a > 1/2 and window w >= 0 with hat-w supported in [-log X, log X], Sigma_rho m_rho Int P_{a-beta}(t-gamma) w(t) dt = Arch_a(w) - Sigma_{n<=X} Lambda(n) n^{-a} (cos-transform of w)(log n), with Arch_a EXPLICIT and the prime sum FINITE. (1) Jump argument: the LHS equals Int u(a+it)w(t)dt termwise (Lagarias identity, absolutely convergent). For a zero rho0 = beta0+i*gamma0 with w(gamma0) != 0, the term Int P_{a-beta0}(t-gamma0)w dt tends to +pi*m0*w(gamma0) as a -> beta0+ and to -pi*m0*w(gamma0) as a -> beta0- (Poisson kernel of height -> 0), so the LHS has a JUMP of 2*pi*m0*w(gamma0) in a at a = beta0. The RHS is real-analytic in a near beta0 in (1/2,1) (digamma, pole terms away from singularities, finite exponential sum entire in a). Two functions cannot agree on both sides of a jump; since the identity is verifiable directly at a = 2 (absolutely convergent Dirichlet series) and both sides are analytic down to the largest depth, the identity holds exactly for a > sup{beta_rho in window} and FAILS below it. (2) Independent confirmation with the exact correction: put the tilted observable in Weil coordinates rho = 1/2 + i*gamma^W. Define h_{a,w}(r) = (1/2) Int hat-w(u) e^{-(a-1/2)|u|} e^{iru} du, a legitimate band-limited analytic Weil test with g(u) = (1/2) hat-w(u) e^{-(a-1/2)|u|}. The unconditional classical Weil EF then gives prime side Sigma Lambda(n) n^{-1/2} e^{-(a-1/2)log n} hat-w(log n) = Sigma Lambda(n) n^{-a} hat-w(log n) — exactly the proposal's prime side. But the true zero side is Sigma_rho h_{a,w}(gamma^W_rho); for an FE-pair at depth beta > a the pair-symmetrized value is Int hat-w(u) e^{-(a-1/2)|u|} cosh((beta-1/2)u) e^{i gamma u} du, whose u>0 branch is e^{(beta-a)u} + e^{-(a+beta-1)u}, whereas the proposal's signed-Poisson pair value has u>0 branch -e^{-(beta-a)u} + e^{-(a+beta-1)u}. The difference is 2*cosh((beta-a)u): the true identity carries a ghost term 2*m_rho * Int_0^{log X} hat-w(u) cosh((beta-a)u) cos(gamma u + phase) du of magnitude ~ hat-w(log X) * X^{beta-a} per off-line zero. This is precisely the X^{|2beta-1|} termwise blow-up / visibility wall recorded in the canon ('the zero-side second moment cannot be read termwise'). Consequences: (a) the claim 'the windowed tilted explicit formula IS prime-computable' (Novelty section, inverting tx_048's negative finding) is false unconditionally — it is prime-computable exactly when quasi-RH(a) already holds in the window; (b) 'locality is cheap: t-resolution of width 1 needs only X ~ e^{2pi} ~ 535' conflates window resolution with detection: certifying absence of off-line zeros at height T requires the ghost to be visible, i.e. X ≳ T^c (consistent with the campaign's measured annihilation threshold L*_ann ~ 1.12 log(t0/2pi)^{0.89}), the same T^lambda economy as the two-thirds method; (c) Milestone M3's headline certificate ('no zeros with beta > 0.9, |t| <= 10^3, from primes < 10^4 alone') and the numerics-plan LP are UNSOUND as designed: they impose the ghost-free identity as a constraint on candidate configurations, which is not the true constraint satisfied by off-line configurations, so any 'certificate' so derived proves nothing; and the planned 10-digit numerical validation would pass (RH is true at tested heights, no ghost present), giving false confidence in a false identity. The formula is repairable only by reinstating the ghost — at which point the 'field' is the classical band-limited Weil EF with a tilted test family, and every escape claim built on the formula collapses.

findings.claim: The claimed new data coordinate ('depth/sigma-profiles, entirely transverse to the t-frequency form factor that all bandwidth ceilings live on') does not exist: every prime-computable observable of the field is contained in the classical band-limited Weil-EF data class, and the depth-CM generator G2 is information-free.
findings.argument: Containment: as shown in Finding 1, the tilted observable at every level a and window w with cutoff X equals the classical Weil EF evaluated at the test h_{a,w}(r) = (1/2)Int hat-w(u) e^{-(a-1/2)|u|} e^{iru} du, which is analytic in the strip with transform supported in [-log X, log X] — a member of the standard test class with bandwidth log X. Varying a does not enlarge the class: the a-dependence enters only through the known multiplier e^{-(a-1/2)|u|} applied to the same band. So the entire (a, w)-family of prime-computable tilted-EF data at cutoff X is a SUBSET of the classical bandwidth-log X explicit-formula data — the exact data class for which the canon's obstructions (DH/Epstein satisfy the EF; o(N)/visibility blindness; adversarial configuration matching) were formulated. The genuinely new objects of the field — pointwise u(s), exact kappa_a, plume geometry — are NOT prime-computable (they require unbounded frequencies, i.e. Riemann-Siegel evaluation, as tx_048 already recorded for the K_a compressions). G2 vacuity: the 'depth-direction complete monotonicity' constraint says the prime side a |-> Sigma_{n<=X} Lambda(n) hat-g(log n) n^{-a} is a finite totally monotone exponential sum. But this function is COMPLETELY KNOWN (finitely many known coefficients Lambda(n)hat-g(log n), known exponents log n); its total monotonicity is automatic from Lambda >= 0 and carries zero information about zeros — the whole a-family {G(a)} is generated by the single finite data vector {Lambda(n)hat-g(log n) : n <= X} under known linear maps, so 'Hausdorff-Bernstein-Widder moment constraints rigidly coupling depth profiles across all a simultaneously' constrain candidate zero configurations through exactly the same finite band-limited data a single level reads. Equivalently: for any candidate configuration, the (ghost-corrected) zero side is analytic in a, so the constraint at all a follows from the constraint near a = 2 by analytic continuation — no new equations. The S5-bandwidth evasion ('TRP certificates read a coordinate that model does not parametrize') is therefore false for everything the method can actually compute from primes; what escapes the PairCeiling format (pointwise positivity of u) escapes it only because it is not computable from the arithmetic input at all. The single-off-line-zero sensitivity (S2 evasion) is a property of the TARGET u > 0, not of any prime-computable instrument: at height T with cutoff X, a single off-line zero perturbs every computable observable by O(hat-w-weighted X^{beta-a} * oscillatory) against ambient fluctuations, invisible below the annihilation threshold — o(N)-blindness reappears exactly where it always was.

findings.claim: The index ladder kappa_a and the whole Pontryagin/OS_kappa defect layer are unconditionally ill-defined below a = 1: kappa_a may be infinite for every a in (1/2,1), and the planned Davenport-Heilbronn validation model (Milestone M2) provably has kappa = infinity at rung one, so no nontrivial finite-defect instance exists.
findings.argument: Krein-Langer theory (generalized Schur functions, Pontryagin spaces Pi_kappa) requires FINITELY many negative squares. kappa_a = #{rho : beta > a} with multiplicity. Unconditionally, finiteness of this count is open for EVERY a < 1: the best zero-density bounds (Guth-Maynard N(sigma,T) << T^{30(1-sigma)/13+o(1)}) allow the count up to height T to grow like a positive power of T at every fixed sigma < 1, and the VK zero-free region does not cover any fixed sigma < 1 at large heights. So the 'integer-valued, nonincreasing' ladder with 'jumps = multiplicities' is unconditionally defined only at a >= 1 (where it is 0); at every rung a in (1/2,1), even WELL-DEFINEDNESS (finiteness) is an unproven quasi-RH-type statement, and the OS_kappa axiom 'under kappa_a = k > 0 a k-dimensional defect space' has no known instance with 0 < k < infinity for any relevant L-function. Worse, M2 plans to 'validate the axioms on Davenport-Heilbronn as an indefinite model with kappa > 0 at rung one': the DH function has INFINITELY many zeros in sigma > 1 (classical — Titchmarsh §10.25; one zero in the half-plane of almost periodicity plus Bohr almost-periodicity/Rouché forces infinitude; same for Epstein zetas with h > 1). So DH's K_a has infinitely many negative squares at a = 1: it is not a Pontryagin model at rung one, and the planned validation is impossible as stated. Additionally the proposal itself flags (failure mode iv) that even the bounded-type hypothesis for Theta_a = xi(1-a-iz)/xi(a-iz) is unverified (xi has order 1 but infinite exponential type; bounded type of the ratio in C+ needs proof). Combined with Finding 2, BOTH advertised 'new generators' (G1 Pontryagin-RP bookkeeping, G2 depth-CM) are stripped: what remains of the OS layer under TRP(a) is the Herglotz/Poisson representation of a positive harmonic function — classical, and the proposal's own failure mode 2 concedes the layer may be 'decorative'.

findings.claim: The central wager (margin propagation, M4) is a known-hard problem in disguise, and a Beurling-type barrier world shows the field's axiom system as designed cannot power it: any inequality derivable from OS_kappa + depth-CM alone is violated by Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer configurations, so M4 must consume an input the axioms do not encode.
findings.argument: Hidden hardness (partly admitted by the proposal, failure mode 1): the ambient archimedean level of u at height t is ~(1/2)log(t/2pi), and pointwise positivity near a = 1/2 must beat Re zeta'/zeta oscillations of size ~log t, while the band-limited prime side controls only the smoothed component; controlling the unsmoothed remainder on windows of length ~1/log T is precisely the campaign's 'Lindelof lock' (bounds for P_X on windows of length 1/log T), never attacked successfully. Any nontrivial m(a-eps,T) >= phi(m(a,T),...) iterates to new zero-free regions, i.e. is at least as hard as improving Vinogradov-Korobov (unimproved since 1958); the designer's own probability is 0.1. Barrier sketch: the generators as axiomatized consume Lambda >= 0, Hadamard/harmonic structure, rung-one positivity, and the FE only structurally (pairing/unimodularity) — no quantitative archimedean-vs-prime rigidity and no integer/exponential-sum structure. Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer (2006) constructed Beurling generalized-prime systems with Lambda_B >= 0, Chebyshev-type prime counting, analytic continuation in a region, AND zeros essentially filling a dlVP-shaped boundary curve — showing that Lambda >= 0 + one-line positivity + harmonic-function machinery alone cannot push the zero-free region below the classical shape. Caveat stated honestly: DMV systems lack a functional equation and entirety, so this is a barrier against the AXIOM SYSTEM (OS-Schwarz + Poisson semigroup + CM prime side, which apply verbatim in the DMV region of continuation), not a strict RH-false lookalike for the full input list; but it proves M2's kill criterion ('at least one inequality not derivable from classical harmonic-function theory') must fail unless the axioms are extended by exactly the quantitative FE/integer input (VK exponential-sum technology) whose absence the proposal advertises as elegance. The residual honest reading — 'an elegant RP-reformulation of Vinogradov-Korobov' — is the proposal's own words for its main failure mode.

findings.claim: The headline numerical evidence ('margin law m(a,60) ~ 0.046(a-1/2), linear in depth exactly as the ladder predicts') is a low-t boundary artifact carrying no information about propagation structure.
findings.argument: The infimum of u(a+it) over t in (1,60) is attained at the bottom edge t ~ 1, where ALL zeros are far (first ordinate 14.13) and u(a+i*1) ~ 2(a-1/2) Sigma_gamma gamma^{-2} = 2(a-1/2)(0.02310) = 0.0462(a-1/2) — reproducing the reported 0.0464(a-1/2) to the digit. This is the Lagarias identity evaluated at one uninteresting point: linearity in (a-1/2) is trivial (every term is proportional to it when |t-gamma| >> a-1/2), and the coefficient is just 2*Sigma gamma^{-2}. It says nothing about the structure of m(a,T) where the ladder's difficulty lives (between-zero minima at large heights, where gaps ~2pi/log T and plumes of hypothetical off-line zeros sit). Presenting it as 'exactly as the ladder predicts' is numerology; the honest check (the proposal's own planned Margin Atlas at T up to 10^4) would reveal the inf stays pinned at the low-t edge.

findings.claim: The first theorem is probably true but its sketch constants fail as stated, and its novelty is modest: it is classical partial fractions plus effective Riemann-von Mangoldt, with unacknowledged prior art on the u > 0 reformulation itself.
findings.argument: (1) Constants: the sketch takes windows of length H0 ~ 1.5 around t0 and claims >= c0 log t0 zeros for |t0| >= 30 via Trudgian-type S(t) bounds. With main term (3/2pi)log(t0/2pi) ~ 0.477 log t0 against S-variation up to ~0.224 log t0 + 0.556 loglog t0 + ~6.8, the guaranteed count is NEGATIVE until log t0 ~ 30+, i.e. t0 ~ 10^13. Repairable by taking H0 ~ 30 (count positive at t0 = 30, per-zero contribution weakens by ~H0^2, inflating C1 accordingly) or by verified computation at low heights — the theorem survives with uglier constants, as failure mode 5 half-anticipates. (2) Novelty: the contrapositive is a quantitative form of the classical Landau partial-fraction lemma (zeta'/zeta(s) = Sigma_{|rho-s|<1} 1/(s-rho) + O(log t)) plus a two-sided RvM window count; assembling it with explicit constants is a publishable note, not a cornerstone. The underlying reformulation (RH iff Re xi'/xi > 0 for sigma > 1/2; unconditional on sigma >= 1) has prior art beyond Lagarias 1999 that the proposal's novelty section misses: Sondow-Dumitrescu 2010 ('A monotonicity property of Riemann's xi function and a reformulation of the Riemann Hypothesis') and Matiyasevich-Saidak-Zvengrowski on horizontal monotonicity of |xi| — so 'no publication studies the geometry of {Re xi'/xi <= 0}' is overstated (the plume/anchoring GEOMETRY may be unstudied, but the positivity reformulation is established folklore). Also minor: the 'Lean-verified first rung' is Re xi'/xi >= N_T/(8t^2) only for sigma in [1,2] AND |t| >= max(2, 2T) (ZeroFree.lean:396), not the full ray a >= 1 as the thesis line implies.

literature_flags: Lagarias, Acta Arith. 89 (1999): exact statement of unconditional positivity on Re s >= 1 and the RH-equivalence — load-bearing for the first theorem; verify (likely correct).

Trudgian's explicit S(t) bound: proposal quotes |S(t)| <= 0.112 log t + 0.278 loglog t + 3.385; Trudgian 2014 gives constant 2.510, later refinements differ — the exact constants are load-bearing for the anchoring sketch and its H0 failure threshold.

Krein-Langer applicability to Theta_a: requires BOTH bounded type in C+ (unproven for xi-ratios; xi is order 1 but infinite exponential type) AND finitely many negative squares — the latter is an open quasi-RH-type statement for every a < 1; the proposal flags only the former.

Davenport-Heilbronn 1936 / Titchmarsh §10.25: DH has INFINITELY many zeros in sigma > 1 (Bohr almost-periodicity); same for Epstein h > 1 — this contradicts M2's 'DH as indefinite model with kappa > 0' (kappa is infinite, not positive-finite).

Missing prior art on the positivity reformulation: Sondow-Dumitrescu 2010 (arXiv:1005.1104) and Matiyasevich-Saidak-Zvengrowski (horizontal monotonicity of |xi|) — the novelty claim 'no publication studies {Re xi'/xi <= 0}' is overstated.
Lagarias ~2005-06 Hermite-Biehler property of xi(a-iz) for a >= 1: recalled from memory in tx_048, never verified in-campaign.

Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer 2006 (Beurling generalized primes realizing dlVP-optimal zero configurations with Lambda_B >= 0): the relevant barrier world for the OS+CM axiom system; verify exact scope (region of continuation, zero-curve shape).
Littlewood: gaps between consecutive zeta ordinates are o(1) (in fact << 1/logloglog t) — relevant to any claim about the large-T behavior of the margin m(a,T).

Baluyot-Goldston-Suriajaya-Turnage-Butterbaugh arXiv:2306.04799 (complex-zero form factor, |alpha| < 1): the tilted-EF data family lands inside exactly this data class — relevant when formalizing the containment theorem proposed as a repair.
